findings.statement: Top convergence rank (rank 1, five evidence streams). Strongly tumour-up in TCGA, tumour-intrinsic after purity adjustment, and protein-level up. Membrane protein (cell membrane, microvillus; UniProt Q16790) with antibody, small-molecule and PROTAC tractability. Drugs as returned: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. HIF pathway gene. Negative: DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (no ccRCC line dependent, not selective) and no somatic driver mutation, so it is a strong imaging/biomarker and antibody-delivery target, not a functional dependency.

Rank 4 in convergence; tumour-up, tumour-intrinsic, replicated in TCGA. Plasma membrane ligand of CD27 (UniProt P32970), antibody and oncoprotein-class (OC) tractable. Drugs as returned: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. Not a DepMap dependency (no selectivity), so the case rests on surface expression for antibody/ADC/cell therapy, not on gene essentiality. Open Targets association is low, so the support is expression and literature, not genetics.

Rank 8 convergence; tumour-up and tumour-intrinsic, replicated in TCGA, with prognosis and grade signal (higher expression associated with worse survival). No drug returned by Open Targets. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency; ccRCC effect is slightly less negative than other lines, so it is a prognostic biomarker, not a validated vulnerability.

Rank 2 convergence; strongly tumour-up in RNA and protein, tumour-intrinsic, replicated in TCGA. Low Open Targets association. Only drugs returned are indirect (ME-344 PHASE_1_2; metformin, withdrawn), mitochondrial-complex agents with unclear target specificity. No DepMap selective dependency. Biomarker candidate, weak target case.

Rank 6 convergence and in the Open Targets top 25; combines genetic association with tumour-up, tumour-intrinsic expression replicated in TCGA. Membrane lipoprotein receptor (HDL uptake), predicted tractable but no drug returned. Cholesterol/lipid-droplet biology fits the ccRCC phenotype. Dependency not selective.

Rank 3 convergence; strongly down in tumour (proximal tubule gluconeogenic enzyme) with TCGA replication and prognostic association (lower expression linked to worse survival). A tissue-of-origin loss marker, so a diagnostic/prognostic biomarker; no drug and no ccRCC dependency (not tumour-up, so poor as a target).

Rank 5 convergence; strongly down in tumour with prognostic association (lower expression linked to worse survival). Transporter with PROBENECID PHASE_4 and PRATOSARTAN PHASE_3 listed, but these are inhibitors/antagonists of a lost gene, so not a therapeutic rationale. Tissue-of-origin loss biomarker.

Rank 7 convergence; down in tumour, with genetic association from Open Targets (top-25 gene). Predicted tractable, no drug returned, no selective dependency. Association-only with downregulation, so biomarker rather than target.

Established ccRCC drug target (everolimus/temsirolimus class), Open Targets association rank 6 in the top list. Not re-profiled here for DepMap or tractability. Listed as an established target that the expression-led convergence list does not capture.

caveats: Open Targets drug stages are reported as returned; tractability is not efficacy. Established ccRCC drugs (VEGFR/KDR, MTOR) came from the disease top list and were not each profiled for DepMap or drugs.
No candidate except EPAS1 shows a selective DepMap dependency, so CA9, CD70, NNMT are biomarker or surface-antigen cases; DepMap 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 biology.
VHL, BAP1, SETD2, KDM5C were not individually checked for dependency or drugs; ranking and association values were not re-annotated numerically except where stated.
Down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PIGR) reflect loss of proximal tubule identity and may partly reflect tissue composition.
Drug_response (PRISM) and STRING interactions were not run, to stay within a small call budget.
